44.en: Why do Snatchers appear in winter? Why are they nocturnal? I have found the answers to these questions.

45.speaker: Gibson
45.en: The Snatchers' vampire-like habits all serve one purpose: avoiding sunlight. They avoid sunlight because their artificial skin is imperfect.
cards: They avoid sunlight|because their|artificial skin is|imperfect.

46.speaker: Gibson
46.en: Prolonged exposure to ultraviolet light causes abnormal growth of melanocytes in the skin's basal layer, producing a skin cancer resembling malignant melanoma.

47.speaker: Gibson
47.en: What humans call sunburn can be fatal to them.
cards: What humans call|sunburn can be|fatal to them.

48.speaker: Gibson
48.en: This link between ultraviolet light and artificial skin should be the key to tracking down the Snatchers. Their artificial skin takes at least six months to fully settle.

Their artificial|skin takes at least|six months to fully|settle.

49.speaker: Gibson
49.en: These findings suggest several ways to identify a Snatcher.

4a.speaker: Gibson
4a.en: 1. Examine the skin. Check for signs of malignant melanoma.

4b.speaker: Gibson
4b.en: 2. Check for an odor. If the skin is cancerous, the cancer cells emit a distinctive foul smell.

4c.speaker: Gibson
4c.en: 3. Check for pollen. Snatchers seem to be hiding in an area where a special cedar called Snow Cedar grows. Its pollen is always found wherever they appear.

where a special|cedar called Snow|Cedar grows.

4d.speaker: Gibson
4d.en: Snow Cedar is an allergen that causes sore throats, sneezing and more.

4e.speaker: Gibson
4e.en: 4. Check for sunscreen. Snatchers wear sunscreen even in midwinter to protect their skin from ultraviolet light.

4f.speaker: Gibson
4f.en: Sunscreen blocks medium-wave UV, which causes sunburn, and long-wave UV, which causes tanning.

50.speaker: Gibson
50.en: Of these clues, 1 and 4 should be especially useful. They must also repair cancerous artificial skin, not just prevent it.
